name: Cloud tenant takeover through token theft or malicious application consent
statement: An attacker steals session or OAuth access tokens, or tricks a user or administrator into consenting to a malicious cloud application, and uses the granted permissions to read mail and files, add privileged roles and persist in the organisation's cloud tenant without needing passwords or MFA again.
weaknesses: Users can consent to third-party cloud applications without administrator review
Long-lived tokens not bound to device or revoked on risk

name: Disclosure of confidential or personal data through staff use of generative-AI tools
statement: Staff paste patient, client or other confidential information into public generative-AI tools to summarise, translate or draft documents; the data leaves the organisation's control, may be retained or used for training by the provider, and the disclosure is neither logged nor authorised.
weaknesses: No acceptable-use rules or approved tools for generative AI
No data-loss prevention on web uploads

name: Interception or tampering of clinical messages (HL7, DICOM) between systems
statement: An attacker with a foothold on the internal network or a partner link intercepts or alters unencrypted HL7 messages or DICOM transfers between clinical systems (EHR, laboratory, imaging, interface engine), exposing patient data or changing results, orders or images used for care.
weaknesses: Clinical interfaces exchange HL7 and DICOM without encryption or message authentication

name: ATM jackpotting through malware or a device connected to the cash dispenser
statement: An attacker opens an automated teller machine or reaches its maintenance port and connects a device or installs malware that commands the cash dispenser to pay out, causing direct cash loss, fraud investigations and reputational damage.
weaknesses: Physical access to the ATM top hat or maintenance port not protected or monitored
ATM software allows unauthorised executables or unencrypted dispenser communication

name: Service outage caused by an expired digital certificate
statement: A TLS, code-signing or authentication certificate expires unnoticed because certificates are not inventoried or renewed automatically, and online banking, APIs, payment links or internal services stop working until the certificate is replaced.
weaknesses: No inventory of certificates and their expiry dates
Certificate renewal not automated or monitored

name: Incomplete inventory of technology assets leaves systems unmanaged
statement: Devices, cloud workloads, ATMs, point-of-sale terminals or applications are missing from the asset inventory, so they are not patched, monitored, backed up or covered by risk assessment, and an attacker or failure exploits the unmanaged asset.
weaknesses: Asset inventory incomplete or not reconciled with network discovery
